messages:
ada: Proposal — we should adopt 4 canonical load profiles + a strict metric glossary so kernel selection / batching experiments are apples-to-apples.
ben: love it. can you list the 4 profiles? short bullets ok.
ada: sure — shorthand names, goals, and a small traffic snippet for the replay harness.
ada: 1) cold-start spike — simulates model/host cold KV-cache (short sessions, ~100ms inter-arrival, high ramp).
ada: 2) chatty short-turns — many concurrent users, short requests (<=64 tokens) latency-sensitive.
ada: 3) long-context few-shot — low QPS, long outputs (512-2048 tokens), throughput-focused.
ada: 4) mixed realistic — mixture of 1/2/3 with prefix caching enabled, matches production percentiles.
camila: important: call out which metrics we measure for each profile. without that experiments are useless.
eli: suggested metric glossary draft:
eli: - TTFT = time from request accept to first token emitted (includes scheduling + kernel warmups).
eli: - TPOT = time per output token (average, measured after first token), used for long-context throughput.
eli: - p50/p95/p99 TTFT and TPOT reported separately.
eli: - QPS = requests completed/sec (doesn't reflect wasted compute from retries or timeouts).
eli: - Goodput = tokens/sec of successful final outputs (excludes retries/partial fallback outputs).
franz: also track KV-cache-hit-rate and effective batch-size distribution (histogram). those explain differences.
ada: yes — add: "KV cold fraction" = percent of requests hitting an empty/uncached prefix causing cache load.
ben: for kernel selection tests we need to pin: model variant, quantization, hardware, seq len distribution.
ben: otherwise the runtime will pick different kernels and results are incomparable.
camila: agree — propose test matrix keys: model (gpt-small/gpt-medium), hw (A100/RTX6000), quant (fp16/int8), profile (1-4), routing policy (latency/cost).
ada: batching heuristics: bench dynamic-batch with target latency thresholds: 20ms, 50ms, 100ms. report achieved goodput and p95.
ada: sample batching config snippet for replay harness:
ada: ```
ada: batch_window_ms: 8
ada: max_batch_tokens: 4096
ada: latency_target_ms: 50
ada: batch_by_sequence: true
ada: ```
eli: for kernel experiments we must record kernel name and kernel input dims for each execution. add that to trace span.
franz: +1. include kernel exec time vs memcpy time so we know bottleneck.
ben: synthetic vs replay: synthetic lets you sweep QPS cleanly, replay is closer to production arrival patterns (bursty, correlated prefixes).
ben: run both: synthetic to get steady-state curves, replay to validate real-world ops (especially KV-cache dynamics).
camila: apples-to-apples rules:
camila: - run baseline and variant back-to-back on the same host with no other tenants.
camila: - clear KV cache between runs for cold-start profiles; preserve for caching profiles.
camila: - use same random seed for synthetic workloading.
ada: logging and artifacts: each run must emit: trace file (kernel-level spans), traffic seed, config, summary CSV with TTFT/TPOT/QPS/goodput and histograms.
franz: regression detection: automated job compares new run vs baseline, flags >5% TTFT p95 regression or >7% drop in goodput.
eli: alert rules: move to oncall if regression persists for 3 consecutive runs. add slack webhook from perf-bot.
perf-bot: deploy-job succeeded: replay-run-1790123456 finished (baseline)
ben: quick note on TPOT calculation: when outputs are variable length, compute weighted average across requests, and report median TPOT too.
ada: action items: camila will add profiles to replay harness (ETA end of week). ben will add kernel-name logging. eli will update metric calc scripts.
camila: I’ll also add a tiny dashboard with KV cold fraction and batch-size histogram for each run.
ada: thanks — once we have baseline artifacts we'll schedule a 30m sync to finalize guardrails for rollout testing. :thumbsup:
